Bombolulu Workshops and Cultural Centre is a program of the Association for the Physically Disabled of Kenya (APDK), Coast Branch that operates several workshops and a cultural center through which it offers social and economic rehabilitation and empowerment of people with disabilities. The mission of Bombolulu Workshops and Cultural Center is to empower people with disability socially and economically through training, and employment linkages by engaging them in financially sustainable provision of competitive products and services.

Bombolulu Workshops and Cultural Centre was established to empower people with disability socially and economically and to enable them to realize their full potential in their lives. The program aims at assisting persons with different abilities to enjoy the right to work; by providing an open, inclusive and accessible work environment, as stipulated in the UNCRPD Article 27 – Work and Employment. Founded in 1969, Bombolulu Workshops was rejuvenated into a self-sustaining program by the Association for the Physically Disabled of Kenya (APDK) in 1987. Originally from Congo, a French-speaking country, Jacque relocated to Kenya and has embraced it as his second home, having spent most of his life in the coastal town of Mtwapa. His vast experience allows him to produce high-quality woodcraft items that resonate with both local and international buyers, providing him with a steady income to support himself and his family.

Beyond crafting, Jacque is committed to keeping the art of woodcarving alive by working with youth apprentices, teaching them the intricate process of creating heritage craft. Through this initiative, he not only passes on his skills but also preserves a vital cultural practice within his community. Mahesh Craft is a testament to Jacque’s dedication to both art and culture, blending his Congolese roots with the Swahili traditions of his adopted home.
